quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm points upward, it signals a right turn. Watch this vehicle and be ready to change your driving.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive under good conditions.
The suggested speed to drive under good conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive under good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed for good road conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but faster is illegal. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and bad weather.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far it takes your vehicle to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These factors change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean?

options.text: You may stop long enough to unload packages.
You may stop only to avoid hitting other traffic.
You may stop to let passengers out.
You may stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may stop only to avoid hitting other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should your wheels point?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parked uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic. On streets without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time. Which vehicle must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right when both arrive at the same time.

questions.question: Your vehicle has no Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) and you need to stop quickly. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pump your brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. This helps you stop fast and still steer your car.

questions.question: You see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal. What should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after checking for other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after checking for other traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Always yield to any vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves left, then right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road will curve to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely drive through these curves.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic signs or signals, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look in all directions, then go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or signals, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Be ready to yield by slowing down, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What is the default speed limit on open mountain highways?
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit on open mountain highways is 40 mph. Always follow posted speed limit signs.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your right shoulder to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An arm extended downward signals that the driver is stopping. Be ready to stop if you see this signal.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to turn on when it slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles use a full lane. Move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic light?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Stop, if you can do so safely.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this won't happen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down at unmarked railroad crossings. Look both ways. If you see or hear a train, stop and wait.

questions.question: How are reversible lanes marked?
questions.correctAnswerText: Double broken yellow lines.
questions.explanation: Reversible lanes change direction at different times of day. They are marked with double broken yellow lines.

questions.question: When does your vehicle take longer to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle takes longer to stop on wet or icy roads. It also takes longer on gravel or loose surfaces.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances.
questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs are green. They show directions and distances to help drivers find their way.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates?

options.text: Cross immediately and as quickly as possible.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Make sure your whole vehicle can fit on the other side before crossing. Do not change gears while crossing.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions down the center of the road.

questions.question: The traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Keep going like it's a caution sign.
Stop before the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down and stop before the intersection when the light turns yellow, if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle. The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road. Always drive carefully around bicycles.
